match.reason: The closest bank point, Supply-side policies, is broader: it mainly explains the market-based and interventionist types with examples, and touches strengths and limits only in passing, so it does not teach the strengths-and-limits idea of this new point.

rejected.title: Strengths and limits of supply-side policies
card: Supply-side policies aim to raise the economy's productive capacity. This can lift potential output and living standards over the long run.
Strengths
they can raise productivity and lower costs, which can allow growth without adding to inflation. They can also improve the economy's ability to compete.
Limits
they often take years to work, because skills, investment and reforms build slowly. They do little to fix a short-term fall in demand.
Some are costly up front, such as spending on education or training. Some can also hurt certain groups at first, so the gains may be uneven.
rejected.remember: Supply-side policies can lift living standards in the long run, but they are slow and may cost money first.

a.q: The government funds a large new trade training program. Which is the most likely result?
opts: A cost now and a gain in productivity later
A quick fix for a sudden fall in demand
An immediate gain with no cost to anyone
A fall in potential output in the long run
a.why: Training costs money now, but skills build over time and can lift productivity. It is not a quick fix for weak demand, because the gains take years.
a.clue: Think about when the cost and the gain arrive.

b.q: The economy is in a sharp downturn, and the government wants jobs to return within months. Why is a supply-side policy a poor main tool?
opts: It usually takes years to have its full effect
It always reduces productive capacity
It only works when inflation is rising
It cannot lift living standards at all
b.why: Supply-side policies work by building capacity, which is slow. They can lift living standards over the long run, so the last option is wrong.
b.clue: Look at how fast these policies work.

version.title: Strengths and limits of supply-side policies
card: Supply-side policies aim to raise productive capacity, the most the economy can produce with its resources. They work on costs, skills, efficiency and investment.
Strength
they can raise productivity, so the economy can grow faster without adding to inflation. Over the long run this can lift living standards.
Time lag
most take years to work, because skills, investment and reform build slowly. They do little to fix a sudden fall in spending.
Up-front cost
many cost money first, such as funding for roads or schools, and some can hurt certain workers or firms before the gains arrive.
version.remember: Supply-side policies can pay off in the long run, but the gains are slow and the costs often come first.

a.q: The government spends heavily on faster freight rail to cut business costs. What pattern of costs and gains is most likely?
opts: Costs now, with gains in productivity years later
Gains in productivity now, with costs years later
Gains in productivity now, with no costs at all
Costs now, with lower productivity years later
a.why: Building rail costs money up front, and the gains come slowly as firms use the faster network. Gains now with costs later reverses the usual timing of a supply-side policy.
a.clue: Think about when the money is spent and when firms benefit.

b.q: Unemployment jumps after a sudden fall in spending, and the government wants jobs back within months. Why would a supply-side policy be a weak main response?
opts: Its effects build over years, not months
It works by cutting the economy's capacity
It mainly works by raising inflation fast
It lowers living standards in the long run
b.why: Supply-side policies build capacity slowly, so they do little for a sudden fall in spending. They aim to raise capacity and living standards over the long run, not cut them.
b.clue: Compare how fast the policy works with how soon jobs are needed.

a.best: Costs now, with gains in productivity years later

b.best: Its effects build over years, not months
